But I'm not familiar enough with the proceedings of that Assembly session to say that it was divided in two, or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything else on that document before I show you the next one?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, we'll have a look at presentation tab 243, master tab 148, which is a report on the work of the Crisis Staff in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, report -- we see such reports in a few municipalities. We just talked about the Krupa one already. These are generally -- the ones I've seen appear to be at the first meeting of the municipal assembly after the war operations, when the Crisis Staff is now supposed to -- or War Presidency, supposed to cease operations and the municipal assembly take over. There seems to have been, in several cases, a report given on what they had done in the interim, and this appears to be such a one. It's dated the 29th of July, so it covers the period from the 15th of May to the 29th of July. I'll just give the usher all of the pages, I'm sorry. It notes on the first page that the Crisis Staff was established in the SDS on the 23rd of December, as we saw in that minute. That, "In mid-May, it was expanded and transformed into the Crisis Staff of the municipal assembly." Again, to replace the municipal assembly, this is the pattern I've described in my report, noting that, as it moves from the SDS organ to the municipal organ, it does add some new members, representative of its wider role as the municipal authority. It says: "It was the supreme organ of authority with all the prerogatives of the Assembly. It adopted all decisions and conclusions falling within the jurisdiction of the Assembly." It then became the War Presidency on the 31st of May, and it's -- okay. Yes, on page 3 in the translation, still on the first page of the report, in the B/C/S, 00349533, just a note on how it worked, that it based its activities on collective work; that sessions were held in the beginning every day and generally twice a week. On the next page of the B/C/S, the first paragraph, an important reference to cooperation with the army; that representatives regularly participated in the sessions; maintained good cooperation and coordination with the Crisis Staff. "All major questions related to the army and police were resolved within the Crisis Staff of the municipal assembly," and notes "This is a period of very successful cooperation between the Crisis Staff and military organs in crushing armed resistance by Muslim extremists." So an example of the cooperation I talked about. The last paragraph on the same page in the B/C/S, 00349534, page 4 in the translation, the report notes: "Certain negative trends which were not compatible with the dignity of the Serbian people; certain paramilitary groups and individuals appeared who engaged in looting, torching, and attacks mostly in settlements, villages, inhabited by Muslims after hostilities had ceased and the terrain had been mopped up, and in breaking and moving into empty apartments." The word for mopping up is "ciscenje terena." I take "ciscenje terena" to be specifically the mopping up of the terrain. The next page in the B/C/S, 00349535, just again describing how it worked; that it discussed and analysed military, security and political situation, and adopted orders, decisions, and conclusions. Page 5 in the translation, same page in the B/C/S, third paragraph, mention of -- dealing with personnel issues in the judiciary, public prosecutor's office, and other -- the administrative organs, public and socially-owned enterprises. "Questions related to the organised moving out of Muslims and the question of the status of Muslim citizens were often dealt with, and conclusions were adopted on these issues at Crisis Staff sessions." So all the various topics that I have discussed in my report. It's nice when they write a report for me and summarise their work. Last paragraph on the translation, first paragraph on 00349536, talks about the role of the Crisis Staff and War Presidency in establishing and equipping the 17th Infantry Brigade. So a summary of their work indicates that the way they -- in which they worked, and the topics they dealt with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next tab, 24 --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask a question? Why was such a report drawn up? Was it for archive purposes or was -- why was this report drawn up? Was it meant to be sent to higher-ups in the hierarchy? Do we know anything about this? Because if I understand you correctly, you found these type of reports in other municipal assemblies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My understanding of this report is that it would be written for the municipal assembly. When it would first meet, the municipality -- it did not meet during this time period. The Crisis Staff/War Presidency took over all responsibilities and competencies of the municipal assembly. When the municipal assembly could meet again, it would confirm the decisions that had been passed in its name, confirmed or not, although the records I've seen, they confirm generally everything. Sometimes they asked for clarification. And I take this to be such a report presented to the municipal assembly, because we also see a list of all the decisions taken by the Crisis Staff and War Presidency, and the municipal assembly would then consider them all. That's my understanding of this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next tab, 244, Your Honour, we'll skip. It's some discussion about a shortage of weapons and training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 245, Ms. Hanson, I'd like to show you, master tab 283. This is a document from the military, dated the 4th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the command of the 3rd Partizan Division to the commander of the 5th Corps, a regular combat report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does it have some reference to the Kljuc Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, and to the themes I had mentioned of some of the military issues. On the first page -- well, actually, I don't believe that's my highlighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one you wanted to talk about appears on the second page.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, second page, 6, state of morale. That's on the second page of the B/C/S, 00954740, at the bottom third of the page 6. Under the question of morale, this report notes that: "Serbian extremism is increasingly present in Kljuc induced by the official organs of authority since the president of the municipality is asking to have his own army which he would use as he sees fit." The president of the municipality was Jovo Banjac, member of the Crisis Staff. I'm sorry, I'm getting confused with the names. We'll see in the other documents the president of the municipality and the president of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Veljko Kondic?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. A few too many names, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us his name again?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veljko Kondic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you see in the documentation anything about that event that was being discussed, or how the JNA reacted to it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of this particular thing, not -- not this event in Kljuc. I'm not ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Let me now talk about the police, which was another topic we've discussed before with regard to the Crisis Staffs, and I'll hand you presentation tab 246, master tab 183, from the 7th of May.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. An announcement of the Kljuc municipal Crisis Staff on the formation of the Serbian public security station in Kljuc. This is, of course, consistent with the 19 December instructions on taking over the police station. This says that the police now wear the Serbian flag and patch on which the word "police" is written in Cyrillic. The Serbian flag is displayed on the municipal building. The Kljuc municipality will be incorporated in the Autonomous Region of Krajina and the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and "therefore, the municipality is automatically required to administer laws and decisions adopted by the Assembly of the Serbian Republic of BH and the Assembly of the ARK." It notes, again, further down, that all decisions is -- and work is carried out in accordance with those organs. And on the second page, which is on the second page of the B/C/S, 00914750, the underlined section in the centre: "All the citizens are guaranteed all civil rights and freedoms, regardless of their religious or ethnic background, provided that they respect the authorities." So the authority -- the Crisis Staff is setting itself up as the authority and demanding respect and guaranteeing rights in return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me go next to presentation tab 247, master tab 202. This is from a Crisis Staff meeting on the 13th and 14th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here, I take you to agenda item 2, the adoption of positions in connection with the decisions of the Serbian Assembly of BH. As you'll recall, there was a session on the 12th of May of the Serbian Assembly. On the second page, under item 2, we see that Jovo Banjac, president of the Crisis Staff, and Rajko Kalabic, deputy of the Assembly, discuss the security situation "in connection with the decisions and reports of the session of the Serbian Republic of BH Assembly." And the Crisis Staff adopted a report in connection with the decisions of that Assembly. So more indications of the communications from the Assembly to the municipality, and the municipal support for the Assembly decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In addition to these minutes of that meeting, did you have some other document referring to what took place in regard to that discussion?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I mentioned, we have a copy of the diary of the secretary of the Crisis Staff, which also has minutes of this meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me refer you, then, to tab 248 in the presentation, master binder number 13. And in the original, this is a handwritten document, so could you refer us to which portions you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first reference is the B/C/S 01399464, and it -- agenda for a meeting of the Crisis Staff on the 14th of May. The items, "the separation of the Serbian ethnic community from ..." it is a handwritten document so some parts are illegible. "Creation of our territory and a transversal - the corridor; borders on the Una and Neretva; division of Sarajevo; access to the sea." Those are all consistent with the strategic objectives. Here it is notable that they do not have reference to the Drina, which was one of the strategic objectives. But I would point out that Kljuc is quite far from the Drina. But this indicates that the strategic objectives, as discussed at the 12th of May session, were conveyed to the municipal level. Other items here are also consistent with the 12th of May session that the -- the establishment of the VRS, the army under the command of the Presidency, also anthem, borders and taxes, those are all mentioned in the 12th of May session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also, from this diary, another meeting of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. If you want to refer to that while we have the diary there.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is on the B/C/S 01399467 and the following page. A note under -- that's not the right page for you. It's 19 and 20. Page 19 in the translation, on item 2 in the agenda, "political and security situation - Telexes." On the next page, in a moment, we'll see what the telexes might have been about. I'd draw your attention to a list of the make-up of the Crisis Staff. President is Jovo Banjac and Veljko Kondic is the deputy president. Also, a lieutenant colonel, Milojevic is listed, as is the assembly deputy, Rajko Kalabic. On the next page, 01399468 in the translation -- in the B/C/S, indication of communications from higher levels. Veljko Kondic read out the telexes from the Bosnian Krajina, and R. Karadzic. Then they discussed mobilisation, including mobilising all Muslims to report. Then I note that the telexes would be photocopied and copies sent to the police, the TO, president of the assembly, an indication of the orders being passed from -- received from Karadzic and from, apparently, the ARK level and then distributed -- passed further on to the municipality for implementation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything else from that before we go on?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's all from that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I intended to skip the next tabs, 249 and, 250, and 251, and go to tab 252, which is master tab 79.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an excerpt from the book of minutes of the Kljuc municipal assembly Crisis Staff. Ms. Hanson, I think we had particularly taken note of items 1 through 3, 10 through 13, and 18 and 19, on these pages.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just like to point out that, for some reason, the pages of this book of minutes were stamped out of order, so the ERNs of the original will jump around. But if you look at the -- if you read each page carefully, they can be put together in the order that they are. There might be a little confusion because of that, and because, of course, the translation sometimes takes less -- is more -- translation covers many pages just because it's more neatly written. But this is beginning on 00573857. Under item 2, we see -- sorry, item 1, a reference to the Crisis Staff of the ARK, affirming the legitimacy of the ARK Crisis Staff. Two, judicial appointments, again proposing judges and prosecutor. Item 3, replacing all non-Serbian personnel in various posts "where independent decision-making is possible and the protection of properties ..." So dismissal of non-Serbs. Under -- at the next page of the translation, at the bottom of the next page in the B/C/S, 00573858, a nice explication -- the Crisis Staff is explicating the relationship between the military and the civilian. "The military authorities will follow the orders of the civilian authorities. The civilian authorities will not interfere with the way they are followed." Then under item 11, which is on the next page, in the B/C/S, 00573859. "Establishment of an agency for the reception/removal of refugees from one region to another." Number 12, "Prohibit the return of families that have departed if those families did so without appropriate reasons." Also mobilisation, a discussion. Number 18, which is on the next page in the B/C/S, 00573860: "The municipal Crisis Staff adopted the decision on the organisation of departure from the area of the municipality. The departure of individuals from the municipality will be organised by the municipal secretariat of national defence." Then the last -- well, I didn't even get it on there. Yes, I'm sorry. Under -- it's a moment where the B/C/S does not follow immediately, but I believe it is 00573874. I'll confirm that in a moment. The Crisis Staff is appointing battalion command personnel, and so on, so more indication of the Crisis Staff appointing military personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have that page in the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, it's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It's the next tab, actually, because it is -- it's 00573882. It's where -- the interruption jumps from 60 to 82. Because that page also contains the 28th of May announcement, it's entered, I guess, as a separate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was -- oh, yes, the previous one was 81, last two digits of the ERN number, and that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The previous one we saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the second one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's all for this session, as I say. That page also includes the next session, but that's another tab.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to skip a couple of tabs, 253 and 254, and take you to tab 255 in the presentation, which is master tab 82. And this refers to the meeting of the 29th of May.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in the B/C/S 00573883 and 3884. First sentence, just to note that the Crisis Staff is in continuous session. That same paragraph, at the end: "The transport of the Muslim members of Territorial Defence to Stari Gradiska has been secured." And under item 3, which is on the second page of the B/C/S, discussing the mopping up of two areas of town - in the original it's simply "ciscenje" - to be carried out by the police. So the Crisis Staff ordering the police to carry out the ciscenje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, presentation tab 256, master tab 83, and I believe it begins on the bottom of that first page. It's a meeting from the 30th of May, 1992. I'll get to you comment on some items on the second page in the English.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This begins in the B/C/S 00573885. I'd note that the unit commander was at the session of the Crisis Staff, and his decision to block the villages of Ramici, Plamenice, Vukova Sela, Krasulje and Kaliska was accepted, with the obligation of calling for the unconditional surrender and surrender of arms. And then, if no resistance is given, the mopping up of the area can be carried out. It is "ciscenje terene." Item 2, which goes onto the next page of the B/C/S, 00573886, that the police carry out the mopping up - again, "ciscenje terene" is mopping up - and according to the plans as set, and to carry out the return of weapons. So there's a plan for the ciscenje terene, mopping up of some towns -- areas of the -- towns, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, let me skip the next tab, presentation tab 257, and go to presentation 258, master tab 85, for a meeting on the 2nd of June.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is, in the B/C/S, 00573890. Notable here under item 1, that the brigade commander reports to the Crisis Staff. And then under (b), the chief of police reports to the Crisis Staff on the operations of the police in mopping up the area, on processing those arrested, and on the security of the town. It is "ciscenje terene," mopping of the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, presentation tab 259, master tab 86. This is a meeting on the following day, the 3rd of June, and in particular, items number 4 and 7.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is, in the B/C/S, 00573891, and on to the next page. Item 4, "the question of the removal of the population." And item 7, the problem or the "issue of prisoners." I would point out that the discussion of those agenda items is missing from the pages of the book. We did not seem to receive them. Some pages are out of order, but the pages that correspond to those agenda items are not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. To the first four items --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first four items, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a discussion of item number 7 regarding prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that is the next page, as stamped 00573892. On the issue of prisoners, the chief of police indicated to the Crisis Staff the problem of prisoners, the greatest problem being their accommodation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have some difficulties in following this. You said the discussion on item number 2 regarding prisoners was at ERN number, last two digits, 92. I couldn't find them that quickly, because under tab 258, it stops at 891. Should I look at the next one? But then I have difficulty --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, 3891 appears twice. One, for the first half of the page, referring to the previous session, that's the previous tab --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- but the tab, the document we're looking at now, it's the same page, 3891, in reference to the session of the 3rd of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's, in the translation, page number 10 at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where, now, do we see the -- agenda item 7 discussed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm -- I take it that there is a numbered translation as well. Would that be on page --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Page 11 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And under what tab do I find that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think the B/C/S for that page 92 was actually behind tab 259.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So we move to the next tab.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've been in 259.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. Perhaps I failed to follow you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had difficulty myself putting the translation together with each session. It's very difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said "I couldn't find them that quickly because, under tab 258 --" Then you said, "Should I look at the next one," but then you had a difficulty -- no, that was me, myself. Well, I'm there, that's the most important.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And to everyone's relief, I hope, we'll skip tabs 260 through 263, because mostly those are just to reflect reports from the police, the army, and the TO, and go to tab 264 in the presentation, which is master tab 91.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could talk about a meeting on June the 6th and June the 9th.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The B/C/S is 00573870. The top of the page, which is from the 6th of June session, on page 14 in the translation, the third item: "The status and employment of Muslim citizens should be resolved on the regional level across the board." Then skipping the next item. "The matter of the organised removal of the Muslim population should be resolved." And lastly, skipping another sentence, the last sentence: "Nothing should be done to the Muslim population in areas where it is not necessary." And still on the same page in both the translation and the B/C/S, the 9th of June session, noting a report on the condition of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. prisoners as number -- as item number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Anything else from that one?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On page 15 on to 16 in the translation, and I'm just checking the B/C/S, 00573871 on the B/C/S, about three-quarters of the way down, "the question of the employment of Muslims" seems to be referring to the earlier decision on managerial posts and important posts concerning property and information. Agenda item 4, in the B/C/S 00573872, discussing the status and the inclusion of Muslims and Croats in the health authorities, and the need to take a specific stand on this issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask one question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This Chamber has understood the case of the Prosecution to be that many of the actions undertaken were actions to make certain municipalities and areas purely Serb. You just highlighted a line which says, "nothing should be done to the Muslim population in areas where it is not necessary." Does that mean that these were areas which were not aimed at becoming purely Serb in this municipality, or is this contradicting, to that extent, the Prosecution's case that the aim in many areas was to make it purely Serb? I tried to understand how, in this decision -- it seems to say, if you don't need it, let the Muslim population, let them -- well, if not be in peace, at least be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are several factors which might --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say it's beyond your expertise, then please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can't know exactly what they mean here in Kljuc and what areas they refer to. But it is notable in -- from these minutes that there are discussions of disarming of Muslims and some resistance to disarming. We don't know where -- what areas they say it isn't necessary. But that might be one of the criteria, because that is a common theme. Another would be -- I'm thinking of, here, also the document we looked at not long ago where the representatives of several municipalities, including Kljuc, said that Muslim population or non-Serb population should be moved out to a level at which Serbian authority can be maintained. And some areas might be more Muslim-settled and less Serb, but there -- in all these municipalities, no settlement was ever entirely, or practically no settlement was entirely Serb or entirely one nation -- one ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You've heard the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I take it that -- well, being aware that it leads to -- it was a question that arose, that to the extent you intend to present any further evidence on that, we'll hear that, if it comes to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I know this is not time to make argument; we'll address that much later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me move on, then, to tab 266, which is master tab 29 -- is master tab 93. This is a meeting of the 16th of June, and I'd like you to mention or discuss items 1, 3, and 7 in that meeting.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is, on the B/C/S, 00573873, and the next page. Agenda item 1, appointing the brigade commander, saying it should be resolved by, pardon me, the 18th of June, noting this is still into June -- yes, sorry. I apologise, I seem to be in the wrong tab. I gave the wrong B/C/S, my apologies. Or did I? This is, by far, the worst set of documents for the case studies. It will get easier. I don't want to see that; it doesn't help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know the date of the meeting is on the preceding English page, but the substance is on that first page you have.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see, I see. Yes. I don't seem to have the B/C/S pages in front of me, so I can't give the ERN.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Items 3 and 7, at any rate, are on 00573861.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know if item 1 would be on the immediately preceding page.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 74. This is where the confusion arises. Yes, item 1 is on 00573874, on appointing the brigade commander, and item 3 is --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 3 and 7 appear to be on 00573861.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. It is a confusion. "The Crisis Staff shall remain the highest authority and will cooperate fully with the military command and the Kljuc SJB." Item 7 on the same page, that "a work group should review the situation regarding managerial posts held by Muslims, and to propose new personnel solutions."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we'll skip some tabs 267 through 271, and go to presentation tab 272, master tab 99. Those tabs we skipped are footnotes in your report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just drawing the attention to the fact that it might be a bit confusing now for Mr. Krajisnik, because the issue under agenda item 1 about the appointment of the brigade commander does not appear in the original under the same tab number, 266, but does appear under -- the original, under tab 265.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The preceding tab, that's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whereas it does not appear in the translation under tab 265, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, it's not. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's a bit confusing, and I'd like you to specifically tell us not only what ERN number the original can be found, but also so under what tab number, so that Mr. Krajisnik is able to find it. But, of course, the Chamber prefers to have the translation under the same tab number as the original is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We do too, Your Honour. This is the last one in connection with that last handwritten document, and hopefully it will go smoother after this one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this one, Ms. Hanson, I wanted you to refer to the meeting of the 26th -- the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 10th of July, that's 00573879, noting the adoption of the decision on the establishment of a War Presidency. So we see the Crisis Staff becoming a War Presidency in July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that same page, I believe in both the B/C/S and English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which tab are we at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is tab 272, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. We skipped several.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We skipped, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: 267 through 271.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 10th of July, I've got that. Yes, and I see that all is in the original under the same tab, at least the 10th of July. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And right above that, on the English page, and I believe also in the B/C/S, in discussing matters in the previous meeting --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the previous meeting. "The question of the status of Muslim citizens and further work employment." The municipal Crisis Staff refers this decision to what they term the Banja Luka regional Crisis Staff, a reference, I take it, to ARK, the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's finish with that one, then, and I'll take you to presentation tab 273, master tab 152. And can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is, in B/C/S, 00575222, a review of decisions, conclusions, rulings, and orders issued by the Crisis Staff and War Presidency -- War Presidency. In the translation it says "the Crisis Staff of the War Presidency," but if we just put the B/C/S on the screen, you can see it's just a hyphen, if that's helpful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I see you highlighted some particular items on that list. Can you tell us about those, please?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I pointed out the hyphen just to show that it's seen as a -- essentially the same body. Yes, there's some interesting decisions here. I take this document to be connected to the report that we saw. In other municipalities, we have seen this kind of list submitted to the municipal assembly for their review and confirmation. There's no indication on this document that that was its purpose, but it's consistent with that. If we look at decisions 12, 13, 14, 16, and 17, they are decisions on judicial dismissals and appointments; 18, establishing a War Presidency; 21, financing the army, paying a sum to the army; 23, a committee for the receipt of war and other booty; 26, which is on the next page, in the B/C/S, 00575223, a decision on members of the War Presidency to -- allowing them to carry weapons and wear uniforms, which I think is indicative of their -- the military role in which they -- that they gave themselves, or they saw themselves as having. On the next page in the translation, 29, reinforcing the infantry brigade. Then the last -- from 31 onward, decisions on municipal appointments and dismissals, or in this case just dismissals; decision on positions that can only be filled by workers of Serbian nationality; and the last item, "committee for the collection of data relating to the population exodus from the territory of Kljuc municipality."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to skip several tabs, 274 and 275, relating to freedom of movement, and they are footnoted documents to the report. 276 to 280 regard dismissal from municipal employment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would like to go to 281, which is master tab 131. This is from -- a decision from the 10th of July, I believe, or the 13th. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the session was held on the 10th, and the date on the published decision is the 13th. This is the B/C/S 00575284. Notable in the preamble, that they take this decision to form the War Presidency, on the basis of Article 2 of the decision on the formation of War Presidencies in municipalities during imminent threat of war or state of war. I take that to be a reference to the Presidency decision of 31 May. As we saw, according to the 10th of June decision, that 31 May decision was superseded by the later decision. But you can see that on the ground, the municipalities -- this municipality, at least, still took its decision to form a War Presidency on the basis of that Presidency decision. Clearly, the War Presidency is replacing the Crisis Staff; it says it's formed instead of the Crisis Staff. The makeup is almost identical to the Crisis Staff, as listed in the 18 May entry of Bajic's diary. Certainly, the essential members, the same Jovo Banjac, president; Veljko Kondic, deputy president. Item 7, Rajko Kalabic, the Assembly deputy is a member; 8 and 9, the head of the police station and the secretary of the SDS; and lastly, number 12, the commander of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me show you next presentation tab 28 --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to skip 282, which is the decision she mentioned before regarding War Presidency members carrying weapons and uniforms -- and wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 283 in the presentation is master tab 313, from the 21st of July. Can you tell us about that one?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The B/C/S, 00914877, a decision that only Serbs can hold positions -- managerial positions or positions where the inflow of information is important, and all places of importance for protecting socially-owned property and the functioning of economic entities. Then they specify, sort of, "all socially-owned enterprises, shareholding companies, state institutions, public enterprises, and the police station." Item 3, similarly, Serbs who are not loyal to the Serb Republic -- Serbian Republic, cannot fill those positions either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, might this be a good time for the next break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. We will adjourn for 20 minutes. We will resume at 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Krajisnik has some query, which I'm not able to understand, just about a specific -- apparently about a specific piece of material. I'm not quite sure who the query is addressed to. I wonder, with Your Honours' indulgence, if he can just put it and then we'll know who the query is addressed to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's very kind. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Especially in the absence of Ms. Cmeric, I'll be a bit more flexible. Please ask what you're going to ask. Would it be a question for the witness or for us or ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I just asked this lady to find me a file. It's an electronic piece of evidence. I gave her a number but I'm afraid we didn't understand each other well, me not speaking English. I have the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sometimes, Mr. Krajisnik, communication is not that easy. I think Ms. Philpott understood that you were looking for that document, and she passed the request to the OTP case manager, and as soon as it has been found and printed, you will receive the copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I did understand it was a practical matter, and I'm grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is another matter before I allow you to resume your examination-in-chief, Mr. Hannis. I indicated before that the Chamber would try to give a decision, an oral decision, in a couple of days on the motion for adjournment. Since the Chamber could not decide the matter before, I would say, the e-mail exchange of the parties was finished, before we knew about the result of that, meanwhile, the Chamber worked hard on a draft decision in writing, because the matter was important enough to have it in writing. I can inform the parties that our decision will be filed this afternoon, in writing. It's now undergoing the final checks on formalities, but the decision is there, and in the decision, the motion is denied. But that's what's going to be filed this afternoon so that the parties are aware of it. Then, Mr. Hannis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think we left off with tab 283. I intend to skip tabs 284 through 288. They all pertain to dismissals of Muslims from employment, I believe, in the municipality, and they're referred to in the report. I would note that 287 refers to Asim Egeric and 288 refers to Omer Filipovic, who were gentlemen we heard about during testimony about Kljuc municipality earlier in the case, and Mr. Filipovic who died in Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 289 is the next one I'd like to go to, Ms. Hanson, it's master tab 349. It's a decision of the War Presidency, dated the 30th of July, I believe.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The decision of the War Presidency on the criteria required in order to move out of Kljuc municipality. We saw one earlier from Sanski Most. And just to show it has similar criteria, under article 1, that "families and persons who issue a statement ... declaring that they are moving permanently from the territory shall be permitted to leave," again, the exchange of real estate or placing properties, at the disposal of the municipalities permitted, under Article 2, but the sale of property is not allowed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In relation to that, can I show you tab 290 in the presentation, master tab 351.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a record dated the 31st of July, a statement by Camil Kuburas, that he is leaving Kljuc permanently and voluntarily. At the bottom of the translation, and on to the second page of the translation, he says that he "has been informed of the order of the War Presidency of Kljuc on the criteria for the possibility of permanent departure of 30 July," and he states that he is leaving Kljuc voluntarily and permanently. And he registers the house that he has in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That concludes our case study on Kljuc. Now, if we could turn to Trnovo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did see under tab 289 that the conditions for leaving included the possibility to take all movable property, although they needed to have an inventory of those -- of that movable property. It doesn't say anything about 300 Deutschemarks. But I had to check first whether this was before or after, but I couldn't find it that quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 300 Deutschemarks that I noted before was from Kotor Varos, and at the moment I don't recall that we had seen that amount specified in Kljuc. If we --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm looking for that tab number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to consult it, but I've not found it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But it would be -- this document would be after anything we saw from Kljuc, because it's dated the 31st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's tab 230, Your Honour, and it was from Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. Please proceed. I'll find it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, turning to Trnovo, I'd like to hand you presentation tab 291, which is master tab number 10. This is from a meeting on the 25th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Minutes of the meeting of the Trnovo SDS municipal board on the 25th of December. We have seen this document at the beginning of the presentation on the receipt and implementation of the 19 December instructions, and just now looking at Trnovo as a whole to see -- they did receive these instructions by the 25th of December. It appears because agenda item 1 is directives referring to organising Serbian people in crisis situations, and the meeting sets up a duty roster, sets up a Crisis Staff. And here we know Glisa Simanic is suggested as a coordinator. He's a character we will see in these minutes, and you'll recall the intercepted conversation between Glisa Simanic and General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And following on that, two days later, presentation tab 292, master tab number 44, another meeting in Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Minutes of the meeting of the Trnovo SDS municipal board on the 27th of December. In the B/C/S, 02280490, the lower half of the page. It notes that: "On the basis of the instructions for organisation of the Serbian people," they name the members of the secretariat as members of the Crisis Staff, along with officials in the municipal assembly, saying that the Assembly will appoint a Crisis Staff and Radivoje Draskovic, who was president of the SDS Trnovo, is nominated for the post of president, and Glisa Simanic was appointed coordinator for crisis situations. This is the document we pointed out last time. The translation reads, although it's Simanic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to 293, which is master tab 451. This is to indicate that their actions are being taken based on the variant A and variant B instructions.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision of the Crisis Staff of the 5th of July, 1992. I would just like to explain something on this document, that -- the heading says "Serbian Municipality of Ilidza Crisis Staff," but the preamble shows it as the Crisis Staff of Trnovo. At this point, Trnovo seems to have -- the Serbian part of Trnovo has attached itself, become part -- fallen under the Serbian municipality of Ilidza, but it is still, as you see -- the commander of the Trnovo Crisis Staff is Radivoje Draskovic, signing this decision. What's interesting here is that it's a minor decision forming a commission for haying of fields, although you'll note under Article 2, it's the haying of Muslim fields and other available hayfields. More interesting here is the preamble that this Crisis Staff decision is taken on the basis of the instructions on the organisation and work of the organs of the Serbian people in BH in extraordinary circumstances, that is, the 19 December instructions. So the Crisis Staff, in July 1992, is still citing the 19 December instructions as the basis for its actions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, I'd like to show you presentation tab 295, master tab 448.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I've skipped 294, Your Honours. It's in her report.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the minutes of a meeting of the Trnovo SDS municipal board, held on 12 February 1992. On the first page of both the translation and the B/C/S, 02280494, one member complains that the weapons of the Serbian people had been distributed in an unsystematic way, that they had been distributed to people who were not members of the SDS, and that individuals had sold weapons to the Muslims. The fact that even people beyond the SDS were getting weapons is an interesting complaint, to me. On the question of weapons, on the bottom of the page, same page in the translation, and the top of the next page in the B/C/S, 02280495, Draskovic says that "a task force has been formed to provide strictly confidential information about the distribution of weapons of which the members of the SDS municipal board will be informed."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's the last item in binder number 6. We'd like to hand around the last binder, number 7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Ms. Hanson, I'd like to hand you -- do you have binder 7?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to begin -- I'd like to begin with presentation tab 296, master tab number 226.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Minutes of a meeting of the Trnovo municipal board, on the 7th of March, noting, in the centre of the page of both the original and the B/C/S, that: "It has been decided to form armed units as follows: A section, platoon, detachment, company, which will be ready for defence at all times."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And next is presentation tab 297, which is master tab 459.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is two days later, a meeting of the Crisis Staff. This is the first -- earliest session of the Crisis Staff for which we have minutes, connected, perhaps, to the fact that two days earlier the SDS said it was decided to form armed units. The first meeting of the Crisis Staff discusses what has been done regarding the organisation of the command personnel. At the bottom of the page - this is all on the first page of the translation and also the first page of the B/C/S - that the Crisis Staff is permanently in session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 298 in the presentation is master tab number 450.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another meeting of the Crisis Staff on the 20th of March -- March 1992. In the centre of the page, "the transformation of the municipality and the local communes is to be carried out." "A decision must be carried out." And then number 2, "activities concerning the defence and the formation of units. Battalion staff according to military principles ..." And then we note again Simanic briefing the Crisis Staff on the formation of units there. He notes that units have been formed in certain settlements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presentation 299, master tab 441, from the 24th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a meeting of the SDS municipal board on the 24th of March, noting, in the lower part of the first page of the translation, and, in the B/C/S, at the top of page 02280273, Radivoje Draskovic tells the municipal board that "R. Karadzic ordered the second degree of alert, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. organisation of duty shifts, guards, keep control of Serbian territory, take the present situation seriously." Those who received weapons "should use them for the defence of the Serbian people." I would note that on this day, the 24th of March, in the Assembly, we had Karadzic's speech saying that soon there will be the single method applied for taking over, and that they will -- he expects them to receive instructions later from the -- at the Deputy's Club. So secondary degree of alert is, of course, consistent with the 19 December instructions. Also, on this page, "Glisa Simanic informed those present on the organisation of the Serbian command personnel." And on the second page of the translation, and 02280274 in the B/C/S, some conclusions of the municipal board that "Muslims should not till Serbian land, land should not be sold, and taxes from farming should go into a specific account of the SDS." So the SDS is diverting tax revenue into their own account.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, on the issue of coordination --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I wonder in this case - because sometimes it's possible - where we've got illegibility in the translation at the bottom of the first page, it could be that Ms. Hanson is able to help us with something which has been illegible so far.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's very difficult handwriting. I can take a look at that page -- at that line, if that is helpful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which B/C/S we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: 02280273, fifth line up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we ask you, Ms. Hanson, if you would be provided with a copy of this page, that you look at it over the weekend, and if you decipher it, that you, at the beginning of cross-examination, could report it to Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. May we then go to presentation tab 300, master tab 212. And on the issue of coordination between Crisis Staffs, the JNA and the government, can you talk to us about this 29 April 1992 meeting.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a meeting of the Crisis Staff on the 29th of April, indicating -- in which Radivoje Draskovic reports on an agreement reached with representatives of the JNA. On the B/C/S, this is 02276137, Draskovic's speech in the centre of the page, bottom of the -- page 1 of the translation, Draskovic says: "We have agreed with the JNA representatives and they will get involved in the cleaning up of the municipality, ciscenje. We have to get crews for APCs and tanks. This is good for psychological effect. Work on psychological and propaganda activities. We went to the government and the Serbian Ministry of Interior. They gave us about 30 insignia for the police, and they agreed to send a request for money, communications, equipment for the police." On the top of the second page of the translation, which is on page 02276138 in the B/C/S, he says: "In discussion with the Prime Minister, we have agreed to take whatever we can in a polite way." So contacts with the government, arranging for getting support, and contacts with the JNA, getting crews for APCs and tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, I'd like to show you presentation tab 301, master tab 462, dealing with the issue of support from the Republika Srpska government. This is a document dated the 30th of April, I believe.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 30th of April, a letter to the prime minister. A mistranslation, again, of -- translation, Djeric. It should be Djeric, not Ceric. But it notes: "In accordance with the agreement made in Pale on the 28th of April, please provide us resources," and the resources include 3 million dinars. So confirmation of what was in the minutes, an indication of an agreement with the government and support from the government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information about what the agreement reached in Pale on the 28th of April refers to?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous document, the minutes of the meeting, refer to going to Pale and talking about getting resources, and doing it in the nicest possible way. And this is a letter requesting it. I would take that to be related.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, tab 302, Your Honour, we'll skip it. It's just establishing the use of a building for the Serbian police force in Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 303, which is master tab number 447.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Minutes of a meeting of the Crisis Staff on the 30th of April. On page, in the B/C/S, 02276142, the municipal board and Crisis Staff are handing their premises over to the Serbian police station, so an indication of the role of the municipal board and Crisis Staff in informing the Serbian police. Further down in the middle of the B/C/S page, at the bottom of page 1 in the translation, one Crisis Staff member indicates preparations for artillery activity, saying "today we will get Pero to observe the terrain so that the locations are decided. From here, you cannot shell Spile, but you can shell all the other villages."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me next show you presentation tab 304, master tab 446, from the 2nd of May.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Minutes of the Crisis Staff of the 2nd of May. Another reference to military preparations. On the first page of the B/C/S, Glisa, Glisa Simanic, as we know, is present, and Glisa says: "Two combat vehicles and two tanks should be brought up." So the Crisis Staff is arranging for getting tanks and combat vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Presentation tab 305, master tab 105, from the 2nd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order of the Crisis Staff relating to freedom of movement, forbidding Serbs of -- male Serbs of military age to leave the territory. Interestingly enough, under point 3, the Crisis Staff says that the SDS will issue permissions -- special permissions for leaving temporarily, an indication, I think, of the overlap of the municipal and party authorities, as well as the Crisis Staff interest in controlling freedom of movement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I see on the Sanction, on the screen, that you also have the seal highlighted in yellow. Did you want to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Similarly, the Crisis Staff, which calls itself the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Trnovo, uses the seal of the SDS municipal board, further indication of the overlap -- of the Crisis Staff's dual role as both a party organ and a government organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, presentation tab 306, master tab 445.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Minutes of the Crisis Staff meeting of the 3rd of May. On the first page of the translation and B/C/S, first speech by Radivoje, saying that there's a lack of artillery crews, "they should get hold of crews for cannons and mortar operators and send them to Kalinovik for target practice." I would note that there was a JNA army base at Kalinovik. Further down, in the middle of the English translation page 1, on the B/C/S, the next page, 02276151, about a quarter of the way down the page, Radivoje says again: "From tomorrow, one bus should go to Kalinovik for target practice with artillery and infantry weapons," and then he notes that they are moving into the building of the Ilidza Assembly and starting the activities for the running of administrative -- administration organs. You know that they actually moved to Ilidza to conduct their business, but claim to be the municipal authorities of Trnovo. On that -- it's a long meeting, with many interesting comments made. Apparently, some personnel conflicts between individuals on the Crisis Staff. But more important comments by Radivoje, at the bottom of page 2 in the translation, and on page 02276153 in the B/C/S, about two-thirds of the way down, Radivoje says: "We are now trying to establish our authority in the municipality. We shall also appeal to the Muslims, not only Serbs. The army is the product of SDS policy." On to the next page of the translation: "Our goals are well known." And then a comment by another member at the bottom of the page in B/C/S, and on to the next page: "We have achieved now what we dreamt of a year ago. Everything that was done, it was done with one objective in mind."

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we know, if the witness can help on this, whether the underlining in the B/C/S was in the original or -- I don't know. I suppose question number 1 is whether Ms. Hanson has seen the original, whether it's in the copy, or just something about the underlining.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not handled the originals of this ERN, so I can't say. But the way it is produced here, it is there -- it appears to be there in this original handwritten version. This ERN is, I believe, the actual originals. But I can confirm that by going to the vault, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if you have no more information at this moment, we'll have to look at that. I don't know how important the underlined points are, or what it specifically would mean, but let's see. Please proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next is tab 307 in the presentation, master tab 444, from the 7th of May meeting.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, I have a question. I would like to ask the witness how to understand what that sentence on page 2, which is "we shall appeal." I didn't really understand what you said exactly, and I didn't follow. "We shall appeal to the Muslims." At the bottom of page 2, "we are now trying to establish an authority in the municipality. We shall also appeal to the Muslims, not only to the Serbs."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, "appeal" in the sense of win over. "We are going to call ourselves the municipal authority, and we shall try to win the Muslims over, not just the Serbs." Is that a clear enough ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you have 307 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 307, the bottom of the page in the translation, at the top of page 02276157, an interesting indication of links to the republican level, where Radivoje, as president of the Crisis Staff, says that "Djeric has promised to send instructions for the organisation of the administrative organs," et cetera. I would note that this is about ten days after Djeric's instructions on the operations of Crisis Staffs were issued. So whether it's reference to that or other instructions of which I do not know, it is nonetheless indicative of look into the republican level for instructions as they've set up their municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next, may I show you presentation tab 308, master tab 229, from the 9th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, notable are the military preparations and the relations with the TO, because by now, the Crisis Staff has set up a TO command in Trnovo. And we see from the minutes, some - what Subotic called minor disagreements - some disagreements on actions to be taken, and Radivoje, as president of the Crisis Staff, sets out at the beginning of the meeting that "the command must obey and execute its tasks." Again, asserting his authority -- the Crisis Staff authority over the TO command. Then in his next speech, on the same page, he notes that they're expecting a transport from the army and the contents should be put in storage. On the next page in the B/C/S, same page in the translation, Glisa suggests bringing up two self- -- I'm sorry, it's Radivoje, still on the same page. Radivoje, on the same page, suggests bringing up two self-propelled guns. And then on the last page, the second page in the B/C/S, Radivoje says that "Glisa should go to General Djordjevic today to procure the two HUMVEEs," so the combat vehicles. We should constitute our organs in Trnovo. So a combination of military preparations and forming their own municipal organs are discussed at the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next is presentation tab 309, master tab 449. It's a list dated the 10th of May, 1992 of members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who are -- what organs those people belong to?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are all members of the SDS municipal board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what agencies were they from, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of them military or police? If you recall at the moment.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know from my analysis that one was a member of the police, but at this moment, without my notes, I can't say which one. So I don't -- I won't say which.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then let me show you next presentation tab 310, master tab 435, from the 11th of May.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another long session with some interesting comments, and indicative of some disagreement between the TO command and the Crisis Staff, because Danilo Golijanin, listed here as one of the attendees, was the head of the TO command for Trnovo. He attends the Crisis Staff meetings, and the head of the Crisis Staff attends the TO command meetings, indicating the overlap and the communication. Here at the -- on page 1 in the translation, and in the B/C/S, at the bottom of page 02276170, Radivoje says: "Tomorrow, we will provide the army with food from Kalinovik. The mobilisation should be carried out via courier on the list and getting mobilisation papers from Ilidza," so discussion about mobilisation. Then in Radivoje's next speech, still on page 1 in the translation, and on page 02276171, in the middle of the page: "War is unavoidable in Trnovo." On the next page in the translation, same page in B/C/S, the head of the TO command says -- the translation -- apparently, the revised translation hasn't gotten into the binders, so I will read what he says in B/C/S. [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, the channel was wrong. The translation was: "I will not give the order to bomb without serious provocation."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then Radivoje responds, "Well, in that case, we might as well just tell the SDA we're going to surrender all our weapons." I take that to be sarcastic. He warns of provocations, and he says -- this is on the next page in the B/C/S, 02276172, he says: "Even though everything is quiet in Trnovo, we will end up living in a Muslim state." So --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me, I've been trying to attract Ms. Philpott's attention for a couple of minutes, but failing, which is the story of my life, really, but, Your Honour, I have about two minutes' worth of report back. I didn't know whether Your Honour wanted, on the items from the housekeeping day, whether Your Honour wanted to deal with them today. It could be first thing Monday morning. I'm entirely in Your Honours' hands on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For several reasons, I have also a list on those issues on which a report would be received in two days, which ones would be dealt with by the end of the week. My problem is it would easily take us a little bit of extra time, and since my next hearing starts at a quarter past two, I would rather leave it until Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm entirely in Your Honour's hands. No problem at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Whatever was said about reporting at the end of this week will then be the beginning of next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We're grateful for the extension, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to go to presentation tab 311, which is master tab 440. This is from a meeting of the TO command on 15 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned, there was overlap of personality and sharing of information between the Crisis Staff and the TO command. We note that Glisa Simanic is present, and that the commander of the staff informed the present parties about the SDS staff conclusions, and lists the conclusions and positions of the SDS Crisis Staff. On the second page of the translation, in the B/C/S the next page, 00949423, also an indication of viewing themselves as part of the Republika Srpska or the -- the Bosnian Serb state. The commander is informed of the order of the SRBH on matters of discipline and disobedience, and the command concludes that "any violation should be reported to the official authorities of the SDS." So the TO command expects the SDS to enforce the regulations of the Serbian Republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document is one that has, I think, several items we want to discuss. I see it's about three minutes till. I know you directed me to finish my direct today but I've run a little bit short. I have about 20 documents left. I would request the opportunity to finish in half an hour or 45 minutes on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll consider it, Mr. Hannis. On the other hand, what we're doing now where we, I would say, went through the material subject by subject, now we do it municipality by municipality. We went through one entirely. Of course, the material, and the order in which you presented it, appears in the main material as well, so by reading it in its subsequent order, so the only thing that's added, then, is that it is presented in a different sequence rather than that it's any new material. We'll consider it, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I make an observation on that? It's only this, Your Honour: That, for example, certainly we can see, on our side, we can see which documents are coming up. What we can't see is which particular bits of the documents are being drawn attention to. We have no particular wish to insist, with respect to Your Honour, that it's done in this way, in open court. On the other hand, we would need to know on the Defence side, very quickly then, what are those passages. So there are other ways of doing that, but simply to throw that batch of documents at us without that steer, that's not so readily manageable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the other ways in dealing with it would be that you indicate by each step -- one way of doing it would be that you make one example of that and say, These are the portions we'd like to highlight, to draw your specific attention to, and then we can read it and then and it's there. Of course, then we miss the comments. But on the other hand --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what I had in mind is we would have no problem with that, Your Honour, but could I please ask then to have that by, say, 5.00 today, which is work in a different way. I'm not pressing for this, Your Honour. As far as the Defence is concerned, we're in Your Honours' hands. We're not pressing for this. We have no problem with Mr. Hannis simply proceeding in the conventional way and completing his examination-in-chief. That is, in principle, the preferable course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may make one last comment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- in terms of appeal. Of the remaining 21 or 22 documents, I think eight or nine of them are new, were not footnoted to her documents, so they're items we haven't seen before. In addition, we did lose half an hour at the beginning of today and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I know that, but that's, of course, a bit included, because you said you would not need perhaps the last one hour and a half, so altogether -- Mr. Hannis, you're invited to provide Mr. Stewart with a copy of the last materials, indicating, if it's only briefly, but by perhaps marking with the yellow marker, the areas you'd like to draw specific attention to. At a later stage, the Chamber might give you an opportunity, if there are really matters of great concern, because most of what we hear now is illustration rather than anything new, but if there's anything that would need very specific attention, but not going through the material as we did now, then you may apply for permission to do so. If you would provide Mr. Stewart with the -- well, the last documents with the highlights, then the Chamber, at a later stage, would like to receive at least one highlighted version as well so that we can work that in our material and are well prepared for cross-examination next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would I be permitted to address the new documents that are not in her report on Monday morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean by new? Because I see there are two kinds of documents. The one is for presentation only, but they are in the original material, because there's usually -- there usually is a reference to the master tab. So to that extent, they are new to the extent that we have not spoken about it in court, but they're not new -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, the master tabs include new material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Master tabs don't include only the footnoted documents to her report. So if it says "presentation only," as I understand it, those are items that were not in her report and we're not familiar with, so they are brand new.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I take it they are used as the basis for your research, even if you made no specific reference to some of them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of the documents that are "presentation only" have come to my attention only after writing the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You may mark those documents that are, to that extent, new, that they have not been taken into consideration by you when you wrote your report. If you are not aware of which documents those exactly are, then Ms. Hanson is permitted to provide the relevant information to you so that you can make up that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think I can tell from our list here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will adjourn. I indicated until now the Prosecution has taken, thus far, some 12 hours and 15 minutes, approximately, in examination-in-chief. Madam Registrar, next week we will sit in this same courtroom? And 9.00. We will adjourn until Monday, at 9.00. And, Ms. Hanson, apart from the exception I just gave to you, although not needed, you will receive the same instructions as I gave you before.
